title: feat: add Liquid D1 decision model via OpenRouter
author: tomdacatto
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #16523

- Adds `liquid/d1` (Liquid AI), no aliases, 65,536-token context, multiplier 1, `paidOnly: true`, no Pollinations GPU. Keeps `/alpha/decisions` and `/v1/chat/completions` unchanged.
- Uses OpenRouter `https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions`, upstream `liquid/d1`. Input costs $0.04/M × 1.055 = 0.0422 Pollen/M; output is zero. Sources: https://openrouter.ai/liquid/d1 and https://openrouter.ai/pricing.
- Adds hidden fallback `liquid/d1:vercel` through `https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/typesafe/v1/systemone`, upstream `liquid/d1`. Reuses the existing client and shared fallback loop. Vercel cost is $0.04/M without OpenRouter's fee; callers retain the public quote. Both routes use Liquid's backend, so this covers gateway failures. Source: https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/sdks-and-apis/typesafe.
- Passed 208 focused tests, 535 catalog compatibility tests, the Enter frontend build, Gen/Enter typechecks, and real local gateway E2E on both routes: Choice/Score/yes-no, structured inputs, streaming, 56k-token inputs, three concurrent calls, cache, catalogs and paid-only permissions. Eight forced OpenRouter failures recovered via Vercel: eight billed events, eight unbilled attempt rows; provider cost and one pack-wallet debit per call reconciled.
- Existing public/free caches and zero-charge chat top-up notices remain. Vercel preserves structured score criteria in legends; OpenRouter stringifies them. Both satisfy the documented legend schema.

gist.headline: A second opinion for decisions
gist.blurb: Liquid D1 joins the model garden for choices, scores, and yes-or-no questions. If one gateway takes a nap, another has the same model ready.
gist.summary: Adds paid-only Liquid AI `liquid/d1` to the model catalog with a 65,536-token context, 0.0422 Pollen per million input tokens and zero output charge, plus a hidden Vercel gateway fallback when OpenRouter fails.
gist.impact: Developers get Liquid D1 for decision requests and chat completions, with the existing endpoints unchanged and gateway failures recoverable through the fallback route.
gist.visual_concept: Polli and the monitor robot sort small choice, score, and yes-or-no cards beside a Liquid AI model tile. Two garden paths lead to the same tile, representing the OpenRouter route and its Vercel fallback without implying two different models.
